name: Apatani homestays, Ziro valley
summary: Family homestays in the Apatani villages of Hong, Hari, Hija and Siiro are the best way to stay in Ziro: wooden rooms, home cooking around the hearth and hosts who can walk you through the fields and clans of the valley.
body: Dozens of Apatani families in Ziro's villages host guests in their homes or in small guest buildings beside them. Rooms are wooden and simple, with heavy blankets for cold nights; older houses usually have shared bathrooms and bucket hot water, while newer homestays add attached bathrooms. Dinner and breakfast are cooked at home, often rice, smoked pork, bamboo shoot, greens and pike pila.

We use homestays for saver and comfort trips alike, choosing better-built rooms for comfort travellers. Hosts can arrange village guides, taxis, forest permission for Talle Valley and Sumo seats out of the valley. Around the Ziro Festival of Music in late September, homestays book out months ahead, so reserve by June.
why: Evenings by the hearth with an Apatani family
Walk straight out into the rice and fish fields
Usually includes dinner and breakfast
price_band: ₹1,500–2,500 per person a night with meals (indicative)

faqs.q: How do I book a homestay in Ziro?
faqs.a: Many homestays take bookings by phone or through travel platforms, and we book them for our trips. For festival dates, book by June. Confirm whether meals and an attached bathroom are included.

faqs.q: Do Ziro homestays have attached bathrooms?
faqs.a: Some do, especially newer ones; many older houses share a bathroom. Ask when you book if it matters to you.

faqs.q: Are meals included in Ziro homestays?
faqs.a: Usually dinner and breakfast are included in the per-person rate. Lunch can often be arranged. Tell your host about vegetarian or other diets in advance.

name: Memba homestays, Mechuka
summary: Memba family homestays are the main places to stay in Mechuka: timber houses near the Siyom with warm kitchens, home-cooked meals and butter tea, and hosts who know the valley, its walks and its weather.
body: Mechuka has grown a network of homestays since the road improved, run by Memba families in and around the town. Rooms are wooden, often on the upper floor, with thick quilts for cold nights. Bathrooms vary: some homestays have attached bathrooms with geysers, others share one with bucket hot water. Power cuts are common, so carry a headtorch.

Meals are eaten with the family, usually rice, potatoes, greens, pork or chicken and butter tea. Hosts can arrange taxis, guides for valley walks, and Sumo seats back to Aalo. In winter, confirm heating and road conditions before you set out, and in October book ahead, as the valley's limited rooms fill quickly.
why: Home-cooked Memba food and butter tea
Wooden rooms with valley and river views
Hosts arrange guides, taxis and Sumo seats
price_band: ₹1,500–2,500 per person a night with meals (indicative)

faqs.q: Are Mechuka homestays heated in winter?
faqs.a: Some have room heaters or a stove, but power cuts are common. All provide heavy blankets. Ask about heating when you book a winter stay, and bring warm sleepwear.

faqs.q: Do I need to book Mechuka homestays in advance?
faqs.a: Yes in October and around holidays, when rooms are limited. In other months a day or two ahead is usually enough. Confirm by phone, since network is patchy.

faqs.q: Is food included at Mechuka homestays?
faqs.a: Usually dinner and breakfast are included. Lunch can be packed for walks if you ask the evening before.

name: Deban Forest Rest House, Namdapha
summary: The forest department's rest house at Deban stands above the Noa-Dihing at the entrance to Namdapha National Park. Rooms are simple and power is limited, but it is the only stay that wakes you to gibbons calling across the river.
body: Deban is the main base inside Namdapha, about 25 km from Miao on a rough road. The forest rest house and its cottages look over the Noa-Dihing to the forest on the far bank. Rooms are plain, with beds, blankets and attached or nearby bathrooms; food is simple rice, dal and vegetables cooked by staff or arranged through your guide.

Booking is through the field director's office of Namdapha National Park in Miao, together with your park entry permission and guides. Electricity may run only for a few hours, so carry a headtorch and power bank. In the monsoon, the road from Miao and the rest house itself may be closed; check current status before you travel.
why: Inside the park, above the Noa-Dihing
Dawn gibbon calls and hornbills from the veranda
Start point for walks and the Firmbase trek
price_band: ₹1,000–2,500 a night for a room (indicative); park fees extra

faqs.q: How do I book the Deban rest house in Namdapha?
faqs.a: Through the field director's office of Namdapha National Park in Miao, along with your park permission and guides. Contact them well ahead, especially for December to February.

faqs.q: Is food available at Deban?
faqs.a: Simple meals can usually be arranged through the rest house staff or your guide. There are no shops, so bring snacks and anything special you need from Miao.

faqs.q: Is there electricity at Deban?
faqs.a: Power is limited and may run only for a few hours in the evening. Carry a headtorch and power bank, and expect no mobile signal.

name: Hotel Gakyi Khang Zhang, Tawang
summary: One of Tawang's longest-established hotels, Gakyi Khang Zhang sits in town with views towards the monastery and the hills. Rooms are warm and comfortable by local standards, which matters on freezing winter nights.
body: Gakyi Khang Zhang is a familiar name to anyone who has planned a Tawang trip: a town hotel built in local style with painted woodwork, a restaurant serving Indian, Chinese and Monpa dishes, and rooms with heaters and hot water. Upper rooms on the valley side look across to Tawang Monastery on its ridge.

It is a practical base for the monastery, the war memorial and the day circuit to Sela and the high lakes, and drivers know it well. We use it on comfort trips. Rooms vary in size and view, so ask for a valley-facing room, and book early for October, May and the Torgya festival in January.
why: Established town hotel with heaters and hot water
Valley rooms face Tawang Monastery
Central for the monastery, market and drivers

faqs.q: Does Hotel Gakyi Khang Zhang have room heaters?
faqs.a: Yes, rooms have heaters and hot water, which are essential in Tawang from November to March. Power cuts can happen; the hotel usually has backup.

faqs.q: Can I see Tawang Monastery from the hotel?
faqs.a: Valley-facing upper rooms look towards the monastery. Ask for one when you book.

faqs.q: Does the hotel have a restaurant?
faqs.a: Yes, it serves Indian, Chinese and local dishes. Thukpa and momos are good choices on a cold evening.

name: Hotel Siphiyang Phong, Bomdila
summary: An established hotel above Bomdila's main market on the highway, with valley views, heated rooms and a restaurant. It is a reliable night's halt on the drive between the plains and Tawang.
body: Bomdila is the headquarters of West Kameng and the natural first night above the plains for many Tawang trips. Hotel Siphiyang Phong stands near the main market on the highway, convenient for early departures towards Dirang and Sela, and many rooms look out over the town and the folded hills of West Kameng.

Rooms are clean and warm by mountain standards, with hot water and heaters in winter, and the restaurant serves Indian, Chinese and local food. We use it on comfort trips for a single night on the way up or down. Book ahead in October and May, when tour groups fill Bomdila's hotels.
why: Central location on the highway for early starts
Valley views over Bomdila
Warm rooms on cold nights at about 2,400 m

faqs.q: Is Hotel Siphiyang Phong good for one night on the way to Tawang?
faqs.a: Yes. It is central, on the highway and used to travellers making early starts towards Dirang and Sela. Ask for an early breakfast the night before.

faqs.q: Does the hotel have heating?
faqs.a: Rooms have heaters and hot water in winter. Bomdila nights fall below freezing in December and January.

faqs.q: Is there parking at the hotel?
faqs.a: Drivers usually park on or near the highway outside. Ask the hotel about parking when you book if you are self-driving.

name: Dirang Boutique Cottages
summary: A small riverside property across a hanging bridge on the Dirang river, with cottages in the style of Monpa shepherds' huts and farm food. It is our usual comfort stay in the Dirang valley.
body: Dirang Boutique Cottages lies by the river a short drive from Dirang town, reached on foot over a suspension bridge. The cottages use stone and wood in the manner of the huts built by Monpa herders, and the garden and orchards run down to the water. Meals are home-style, using vegetables and fruit from the farm when in season.

It suits travellers who want quiet and character rather than a big hotel. Dirang Dzong, the hot springs and the National Research Centre on Yak are short drives away, and Sela Pass is about 2 hours up the road. Cottages are limited, so book early for October and spring, and expect cold nights in winter.
why: Riverside cottages reached by a hanging bridge
Farm food and orchard setting
Quiet base for Dirang Dzong, Sangti and Sela

faqs.q: Can cars reach Dirang Boutique Cottages?
faqs.a: Cars stop near the river, and you walk across a hanging bridge to the cottages, a short distance. Staff help with luggage. Tell them if anyone in your group has mobility needs.

faqs.q: Are meals included at Dirang Boutique Cottages?
faqs.a: Meal plans vary; many guests take dinner and breakfast at the property, as there are few restaurants nearby. Confirm when you book.

faqs.q: Is it cold at Dirang Boutique Cottages in winter?
faqs.a: Yes. Dirang is at about 1,600 m and nights near the river are cold from December to February. Ask about heaters and carry warm layers.

name: Siiro Resort, Ziro
summary: A pine-wood resort in Siiro village on the edge of the Ziro valley, with private rooms, attached bathrooms and views over the paddies. It is the most comfortable place we know in Ziro and books out early for the music festival.
body: Siiro Resort stands on a slope above the fields near Siiro, one of the Apatani villages of the Ziro valley, a short drive from Hapoli. Rooms and cottages are built largely of wood, with attached bathrooms and hot water, and the dining room serves Apatani, Indian and Chinese dishes. The setting among pines gives quiet mornings and good walks into the fields below.

For travellers who prefer a hotel-style room to a family homestay, it is the natural choice, and we use it on comfort and signature trips. Around the Ziro Festival of Music in late September it fills months ahead, so book early. Ask your hosts to arrange a village guide for Hong or Hari.
why: Most comfortable rooms in the Ziro valley
Pine setting above Apatani paddies
Attached bathrooms with hot water

faqs.q: How far is Siiro Resort from Hapoli?
faqs.a: A short drive of 15–20 minutes from Hapoli, Ziro's market town. The resort can arrange taxis, and village guides for Hong, Hari and Siiro.

faqs.q: Is Siiro Resort open during the Ziro Festival of Music?
faqs.a: Yes, and it is one of the first places to fill. Book by early summer for festival dates in late September.

faqs.q: Does Siiro Resort serve local food?
faqs.a: Yes, the kitchen serves Apatani dishes alongside Indian and Chinese food. Ask in advance if you want a full Apatani meal.

name: Vivanta Tawang
summary: A Taj-group hotel that opened in December 2023 a short drive from Tawang Monastery. Heated rooms, a full restaurant and mountain views make it the most comfortable stay in Arunachal, and our signature base for Tawang.
body: Vivanta Tawang, run by the Indian Hotels Company under its Vivanta brand, brought international-standard hotel comfort to Tawang for the first time. Rooms are heated, with large windows towards the hills, and the hotel has a restaurant serving Monpa dishes alongside Indian and international food. Service follows the Taj group's usual standards.

It is a short drive from Tawang Monastery and the town centre, and the hotel can arrange vehicles for Sela, the high lakes and other day trips, subject to permits. For signature trips we pair it with Rungkhung Village Resort in Dirang. Book well ahead for October, May and the Torgya festival in January.
why: The most comfortable hotel in Arunachal
Heated rooms on freezing Tawang nights
Taj-group service and dining

faqs.q: When did Vivanta Tawang open?
faqs.a: It opened in December 2023, the first Taj-group hotel in Arunachal Pradesh.

faqs.q: How far is Vivanta Tawang from Tawang Monastery?
faqs.a: A short drive of 10–20 minutes, depending on traffic in town. The hotel can arrange a car for monastery visits and day trips.

faqs.q: Does Vivanta Tawang have heating?
faqs.a: Yes, rooms are heated, which makes a real difference from November to March when Tawang nights fall well below freezing.

name: Rungkhung Village Resort, Dirang
summary: A resort among kiwi and orange orchards in the Dirang valley, part of Summit Hotels' Signature Collection, with valley-facing rooms and polished service. It is the most comfortable stay between Bomdila and Tawang.
body: Rungkhung Village Resort sits on a slope above the Dirang river, surrounded by orchards, a short drive from Dirang town. Rooms face the valley, with wood finishes, heating and modern bathrooms, and the restaurant serves Monpa, Indian and international food. It is a good place to slow down for two nights before the climb to Sela and Tawang.

From here, Dirang Dzong, the hot springs, Sangti valley and the yak research farm are easy outings, and the drive over Sela to Tawang takes about 5–6 hours. We use it on signature trips, often paired with Vivanta Tawang. Book early for October and spring.
why: Most polished stay in the Dirang valley
Orchard setting with valley views
Ideal acclimatisation stop before Sela and Tawang

faqs.q: Is Rungkhung Village Resort good for acclimatisation?
faqs.a: Yes. Dirang is at about 1,600 m, so two nights here before Tawang at about 2,670 m and Sela at about 4,170 m helps your body adjust.

faqs.q: How far is Rungkhung from Tawang?
faqs.a: About 135–145 km over Sela Pass or through the Sela Tunnel, roughly 5–6 hours depending on weather and stops.

faqs.q: Does Rungkhung Village Resort have heating?
faqs.a: Rooms are heated in winter. Nights in Dirang are cold from December to February.
